solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A meal a day's included, correct?

indicators.note: the day is included, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a dish is a meal or course served up
Mon is the usual short form of Monday, a day of the week; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether eating one meal every day counts as the right regime.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone in the sense of rebuking or reprimanding them is a synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Military HQ bombed as may be harbouring resistance

indicators.note: harbouring means the scrambled letters hold the resistance symbol inside them
bombed means the letters of as may be are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: A military headquarters may be bombed even though it shelters the resistance fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombed' turns AS MAY BE into AMYBASE, which harbours R after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An army base is a military installation where forces are stationed and commanded.

clue.text: Perrin's boss in company that pays little

indicators.note: the boss goes in, placed inside the word for company

parts.note: a mob is a crowd or company of people
CJ was Reggie Perrin's boss in the British TV sitcom The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin

explanation.surface: Reggie Perrin's boss works in a firm that pays its staff badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin was a 1970s BBC sitcom; CJ was the hero's pompous boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is a slang term for a low-paid, low-status, dead-end job, as in fast-food work.

clue.text: Sweating over running in rising sun

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in, inside the turned-round sun
in a down clue rising means the word sun is read from bottom to top, backwards
running means the letters of over are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sweating from running under a rising sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' reads as jogging in the heat, but it is the anagram signal, and 'rising' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweating in the figurative sense of being anxious or on edge is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Bar sinks when inverted

indicators.note: inverted in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it, so sinks means pots

explanation.surface: A bar sinks when turned upside down, like a metal bar dropped into water.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to prevent or block them, a synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Greek characters in stone and rock

indicators.note: the Greek letters go in, placed inside the abbreviation for stone

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight of fourteen pounds
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so more than one makes chis

explanation.surface: Greek letters carved into stone and rock, like an ancient inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight unit of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a type of metamorphic rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: With me in tow, dance the hustle

indicators.note: in tow means the second piece trails along behind the first

parts.note: the conga is a dance done in a long line

explanation.surface: Someone joins a conga line, then the dance becomes the Hustle, the disco dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hustle' looks like the 1970s disco dance, but here it means a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustle is a fraud or swindle, the same as a con trick played on a mark.

clue.text: Home help returned to protect one's country

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: to protect means the turned-round help goes round the other piece, guarding it
returned means the word for help is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: aid means help
one's is written as ones

explanation.surface: A domestic helper goes back home to protect their own country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a country of thousands of islands in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Hear nurses butt in

indicators.note: nurses means holding the other piece inside as a nurse holds a baby

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case, so hear means try
a butt end is the end of something

explanation.surface: Someone is told to listen to the nurses and stop interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt in' looks like a phrase meaning interrupt, but 'in' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is fashionable, the current vogue, which is what trendy means.

clue.text: Trouble over door tampered with by second most important servant

indicators.note: over signals the word for trouble is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in trouble

indicators.note: the word door is tampered with, its letters rearranged

parts.note: mo is informal for a moment or second, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: Some trouble over a door that was tampered with, blamed on the second-ranking servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second most important' looks like one phrase, but 'second' belongs to the wordplay and 'most important servant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A majordomo is the chief steward of a great household, the head of the servants.

clue.text: Broken hammer?

definitions.meaning: broken in spirit means overwhelmed, defeated by emotion
to hammer an opponent is to beat or defeat them thoroughly

explanation.surface: A hammer that is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcome means both emotionally overwhelmed and to beat or prevail over, matching the two senses.

clue.text: For one horse, backward shove

indicators.note: backward means the two pieces are read in reverse order, back to front

parts.note: eg, for example, means 'for one'
a dun is a horse of a greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: One horse gives another a shove backwards, perhaps in a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle push or prod, a light shove with the elbow.

clue.text: Scholar blessing monkey

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate and so a scholar
a boon is a blessing or benefit

explanation.surface: A scholar gives a blessing to a monkey, like a priest at an animal service.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large ground-dwelling African and Arabian primate, one kind of monkey.

clue.text: I refuse to return, admitting mum was left

indicators.note: admitting means letting the word for mother in, placing it inside
to return means the word for one who refuses is written backwards

parts.note: someone who says 'I refuse' is a denier, one who denies
ma is an informal word for mother, as is mum

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go back home, even though their mum is there, and so they stayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I refuse' is what a denier says, so the phrase stands for the person refusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained in the sense of stayed behind or was still there after others went is a synonym of was left.

clue.text: Author to appear unsteady through drink

indicators.note: the swaying goes through the word for drink, inside it

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol heavily
to roll is to sway and lurch, appearing unsteady on the feet

explanation.surface: A writer seems to wobble about after drinking too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian English novelist, writer of the Barsetshire novels.

clue.text: 4 more than one 6

parts.note: the answer to 4 down is the word stop; to squash a protest is to stop it
6 down is a con game, a swindle; more than one of them are rackets

explanation.surface: Cross-references to two other answers, read as an arithmetic puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on two other answers: 4 down (STOP) gives SQUASH, and 6 down (CON GAME) in the plural gives RACKETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash rackets is the full, formal name of the indoor racket-and-ball game usually just called squash.

clue.text: Cold rain, cloud, winds

indicators.note: winds is a verb here: the letters of rain and cloud are wound around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bleak weather report: cold rain, cloud and wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' reads as a noun in the weather list, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold of manner, unfriendly and lacking warmth, is what not cordial means.

clue.text: Yes, I'm worried about inflamed back problem

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the word for inflamed
worried means the letters of yes and I'm are shaken up and rearranged

parts.note: lit means set alight, inflamed

explanation.surface: A patient frets that an inflamed spine is a serious back problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns YES I'M into MYEIS, which goes about LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Myelitis is inflammation of the spinal cord, a medical problem of the back.

clue.text: Free burst lip for cutting remark

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are cutting into the word for remark, sitting inside it

parts.note: a commentary is a series of remarks or observations

indicators.note: a burst lip is split open, so the letters of lip are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a burst lip gets it in return for a cutting remark, a free punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting remark' reads as a barbed comment, but 'cutting' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Complimentary means given without charge, as with complimentary tickets.

clue.text: Burning up after grasping snake

indicators.note: after means the turned-round word comes after the word for grasping

parts.note: mean means stingy and grasping with money

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: red-hot, burning things glow red

explanation.surface: Something burning rises after a snake has been caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping snake' reads as seizing a snake; 'grasping' is MEAN, and 'snake' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To snake is to wind or wander along a twisting course, as a river does.

clue.text: Darling's upset over a failure

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is a term for a darling; the 's stands for 'is'
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a can mean per, as in 'ten pounds a day'

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is distraught over a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, a loser or a washout.

clue.text: Sailor given bill, plus 40 per cent for using calculator

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
ac is short for account, which is a bill

indicators.note: 40 per cent of a five-letter word is its first two letters, so that share is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a bill with a 40 per cent surcharge for using a calculator.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires, used for doing arithmetic by hand.

clue.text: Local map-makers will keep off island

parts.note: the local is a British name for one's neighbourhood pub, and a bar is a pub
food that is off has gone bad
OS is the Ordnance Survey, the British national mapping agency

explanation.surface: The neighbourhood pub's map-makers will avoid an island, as if planning a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's regular nearby pub; the Ordnance Survey (OS) makes Britain's official maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean island nation in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Bloke finishes in the civil service

parts.note: bloke and chap are both informal words for a man

indicators.note: finishes in means the closing letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A man ends up working in the civil service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'civil service' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'service' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapel can mean a religious service held in a chapel, as in going to chapel on Sunday.

clue.text: Piano allowed to introduce a flute

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: to introduce means bringing a into the word for allowed, inside it

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A pianist is allowed to bring in a flute player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flute' looks like the instrument but means a groove or fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute is a groove or fold, as in fluted columns or fabric, so a pleat is one.

clue.text: University in publication about island

indicators.note: the university abbreviation goes in, inside the turned-round word
about means the word for publication is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: A university features in a magazine article about an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is an island in the western Pacific, a US territory in the Marianas.

clue.text: Unfinished version of 'Relax' — D minor

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for relax loses its final letter

parts.note: to chill is to relax, take it easy

explanation.surface: A musician plays an incomplete arrangement of the song 'Relax' in the key of D minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relax' was a Frankie Goes to Hollywood hit, which makes 'D minor' look like a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is someone under legal age, which is to say a youngster or offspring.

clue.text: Crack troops in alien kit

indicators.note: the joke and the soldiers go in, inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the alien of the film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
a crack is a wisecrack, a witty quip
troops are soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Elite troops kitted out in alien gear, like a science fiction battle scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack troops' reads as elite soldiers, but 'Crack' is a joke on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is the gear or equipment needed for an activity, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Screw unfortunately gets turned, extremely risky

indicators.note: gets turned means the word for unfortunately is turned round, back to front

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: A screw unfortunately gets turned too far, which is extremely risky for a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is old British slang for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a screw is a person's pay or wages, as in a decent screw.

clue.text: Former international body's without worth

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the body's letters go around the word for worth

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is an international body, and the 's adds an S
merit is worth or value

explanation.surface: A former international organisation is described as having no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a retired professor or official who keeps the title, so it means one-time or past holder.
